ruling.recommended_action: Escalate to a human reviewer: obtain the full GPS trace for the uncovered stretch before 09:20:45 and any verified road-usage data for the driven path, then decide the RD-2 refund on the escalated fare.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider complains the driver deviated and the meter ran to 12 km against a 7.2 km estimate, asking for the extra distance back. On a metered RydeTAXI trip the extra distance does carry into the fare, so RD-2 could refund Σ(unexempt extra km) × (fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km) = $17.16 ÷ 12.17 km = $1.4100/km [F5][F7]. Applied to the one measured off-route segment (4.15 km extra [F4]) that would be 4.15 × $1.4100 = $5.85, but that arithmetic presumes the segment is unexempt and that the record is complete enough to compute — neither is settled [F1][F4][RD-2].

RD-1 requires each off-route segment to pass RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 before any refund; here only one segment is even measurable, and the trace marks the trip-coverage check failed: the GPS trace ends 4 min 0 s before drop-off, so any further deviation in the final stretch is invisible and cannot be measured [F1][RD-1]. The measured excess of $7.04 over 4.99 km [F5] therefore cannot be fully attributed to segments reviewed under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5, and I cannot state a refund amount on this record.

RD-4 does not excuse the segment either: the traffic facts show merely band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Eu Tong Sen Street and Sentosa Gateway, and no incident at all [F12][F13][F14]. Band 3 is not a band-1/band-2 record, and in any case a band alone does not exempt a segment under RD-4 — only an incident on the replaced optimal route would [F12][F14][RD-4]. Weather was fair [F15].

RD-5 consent is absent on this record and cannot be decided: the driver's post-trip statement that "the GPS sent me; it rerouted" is a claim, not rider consent, and a verbal-agreement claim does not establish consent; the only chat is two pre-pickup logistics messages with no route agreement anywhere [F8][F9][F11][RD-5]. Because a segment's exemption turns on whether an agreed route can be tied to the driven path and the record carries no road names for the driven path, that element is undetermined rather than counted [F11][RD-5].

The safety screen is clean: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint; the messages are logistics only and nothing in the file alleges threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks or dangerous driving, so no SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 screen triggers [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. The driver's profile (1 upheld dispute in 90 d, route disputes 0 [F17]) would at most support the RD-6 add-on if this case were upheld; it cannot establish the deviation itself and is not used to decide anything here [F16][F17][RD-6].
